verdict.summary: You can create a Dropbox app and connect your own account in minutes, and invited users can connect while the app is still in Development status. Dropbox only reviews your production request once 50 users have linked the app. At that point you have two weeks to get approved before Dropbox stops new users from linking. The review checks branding, the privacy policy and whether your scopes match what the app does.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gates 1-2; 2-4 hours to prepare the production request (privacy policy, icon, branding, scope justification)
verdict.approval_wait: None for you or test users. Production review starts only after 50 linked users; an old Dropbox support page says requests are answered in 'a few business days', but that may be out of date

gates.name: Development status (your own account)
gates.unlocks: Connect your own Dropbox account through your app and test API calls. The App Console can also generate an access token for your account.
limits: New apps start in Development status and can only connect to the creator's account until you enable additional users
Access tokens are short-lived (the response includes expires_in). You only get a refresh token if the authorization URL sets token_access_type=offline

gates.name: Development status with 'Enable additional users'
gates.unlocks: Other Dropbox users can link the app without review. This is enough for demos, hackathons, staging and internal tools.
limits: Up to 500 Dropbox users in total can link a Development-status app
Once 50 users have linked, you have two weeks to apply for and receive production approval. After that, new linking is frozen
A community answer says Development vs. production status does not change token expiry
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes (one click in the App Console)

gates.name: Production status
gates.unlocks: Removes the Development-status user caps so any Dropbox user can link the app
limits: Dropbox does not review a production request until the app has linked at least 50 users, unless you use 'Request early review' with evidence
Dropbox may deny the request at its discretion. If denied, you get feedback and can fix the issues and resubmit
After production approval you cannot rename the app yourself; you have to ask Dropbox through the developer contact page
gates.time_to_reach: Submit once you are near 50 linked users (or earlier via 'Request early review'). An old support page says a decision comes in a few business days

steps.title: Sign in to the Dropbox App Console
steps.detail: Go to the App Console and sign in with the Dropbox account that will own the app (you get redirected to login if you are signed out). Accept the Dropbox Developer Terms.
gotchas: When you accept the Developer Terms for a company, they bind the organization. The person creating the app should have authority to accept them on its behalf.

steps.title: Create the app and choose the permission type
steps.detail: Create a new app and choose either 'App folder' (the app can only see its own folder) or 'Full Dropbox' (the user's whole Dropbox). Name the app after your product.
gotchas: You cannot change the permission type later. To switch, you have to delete the app and create a new one.
Production review checks whether Full Dropbox is justified. Choose App folder if it is enough.
The app name cannot include 'Dropbox', any Dropbox product name, or anything that sounds similar.

steps.title: Pick scopes on the Permissions tab
steps.detail: An agent can list the endpoints your app calls and map each one to the scope its reference page names. You then tick only those scopes on the app's Permissions tab. If the authorization request has no scope parameter, the consent page asks for every scope ticked on this tab.

values.label: Typical scopes
values.value: account_info.read, files.metadata.read, files.content.read (add .write variants only if needed)

gotchas: Composio's default scope list is broad (it includes contacts and file_requests scopes). Trim it, because production review flags permissions broader than what the app does.
If you plan broader permissions that are not built yet, mention them in the production request.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI
steps.detail: On the app's Settings page, in the OAuth 2 section, add the Composio callback URL under Redirect URIs. Dropbox requires an exact match.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Non-localhost redirect URIs must use HTTPS.
Composio's catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but the research probe used a v3 callback path. Copy the exact URL your Composio auth config shows.

steps.title: Copy the app key and secret into a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the App key and App secret from the Settings page into a custom Dropbox auth config in Composio, and set the same scopes you ticked on the Permissions tab. Make sure the authorization request sets token_access_type=offline so Dropbox issues a refresh token.
gotchas: Without token_access_type=offline you only get short-lived access tokens and no refresh token.
Refresh tokens don't expire until revoked, and a refresh request does not return a new refresh token. Keep the original.

steps.title: Test the connection with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, approve it on Dropbox's consent page, and call a simple endpoint such as the current account lookup. Then check that refreshing the token works.
gotchas: An 'unknown_client_id' error page means the app key is wrong or was not saved in the auth config.

steps.title: Enable additional users for testers
steps.detail: On the app's Settings page, click 'Enable additional users' so people other than you can link the app while it stays in Development status.
gotchas: The cap is 500 linked users. Once 50 users link, a two-week clock starts: get production approval before it runs out, or new linking freezes.

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy and branding copy
steps.detail: An agent can draft a privacy policy for this app that says what Dropbox data you collect, how you use and share it, and how you secure access tokens (HTTPS in transit). It can also draft the app description and publisher text so they follow the branding guide.
gotchas: Marketing must not suggest that Dropbox partners with or endorses you. You can say you are an API developer.
Dropbox rejects apps that break the branding guidelines or the terms.

steps.title: Fill in branding fields and upload the icon
steps.detail: On the app's Branding settings in the App Console, set the app name, publisher, description, website URL and icons. The icon appears on the authorization page and in each user's connected-apps list, and Dropbox requires it for the production request.
gotchas: The logo must not look like a Dropbox logo or include Dropbox wording.
Settle on the final name now. After production approval you cannot rename the app without asking Dropbox.

steps.title: Submit the production request
steps.detail: From the app's info page in the App Console, apply for production. Explain how the app uses the API, justify each scope and the permission type, and include your privacy policy. If you have fewer than 50 linked users, use the 'Request early review' field and give evidence.
gotchas: Requests from apps with fewer than 50 linked users are not reviewed unless you request early review.

steps.title: Wait for Dropbox's decision
steps.detail: Dropbox approves or denies the request. If it is denied, fix the issues in the feedback and resubmit. An older support page says replies come within a few business days.
gotchas: Submit well before the two-week window that starts at 50 linked users runs out.

requirements.item: Authority to accept the Developer Terms for your organization
requirements.detail: The terms bind the organization when you accept them on its behalf.
The redirect_uri must exactly match one registered in the App Console. Non-localhost URIs must use HTTPS.

requirements.item: One app key per distinct app
requirements.detail: If you build a wrapper or framework, each downstream developer registers their own app key.

requirements.item: Each user signs in through Dropbox's own login page
requirements.detail: You may not use one account's login or a single access token to give many users access to one Dropbox account.
It must clearly say what user data you collect and how you use and share it.
No 'Dropbox' in the name, no Dropbox-like logo, no claim of partnership. You also need an uploaded app icon.
Request no more than the app needs, and justify Full Dropbox if you use it.

requirements.item: At least 50 linked users, or an early-review request
requirements.detail: Dropbox only reviews production requests once 50 users have linked, unless you request early review.
Use HTTPS in transit and report any suspected breach to Dropbox promptly.
Dropbox excludes apps that promote copyright infringement, fetch content without rights, or run publicly searchable file-sharing networks.

scopes.effect: Read or write file contents. Production review checks that these match what the app actually does. Dropbox publishes no sensitivity tiers for scopes.
List and manage file metadata. Request write only if the app needs it.
Included in Composio's defaults. Remove them unless the app uses them, because over-requesting can hurt production review and make users decline.
Basic account details. This is a low-risk scope most apps need.
OpenID Connect identity scopes listed in Dropbox's discovery document.

scopes.scope: Permission type: Full Dropbox (vs. App folder)
scopes.effect: Full Dropbox gives access to the user's whole Dropbox and gets extra scrutiny in review. You cannot change the permission type after creating the app.

blockers.symptom: New users can't link the app after it passes 50 users
blockers.cause: The two-week window that starts at 50 linked users ran out before production approval
blockers.fix: Submit the production request as you approach 50 users, or earlier using 'Request early review'.

blockers.cause: The app name or logo uses Dropbox wording or looks like Dropbox, or the marketing implies a partnership
blockers.fix: Rename the app or redesign the icon to follow the branding guide, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Production request denied for over-broad permissions
blockers.cause: The app asks for scopes or Full Dropbox access its features don't use
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes on the Permissions tab and explain planned features in the request. Switching from Full Dropbox to App folder means creating a new app.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error during authorization
blockers.cause: The callback URL is not registered exactly, or a non-localhost URI uses http
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the OAuth 2 Redirect URIs field.

blockers.cause: The app key in the auth config is wrong
blockers.fix: Copy the App key from the App Console Settings page again.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after a few hours
blockers.cause: No refresh token was issued because token_access_type=offline was missing
blockers.fix: Add token_access_type=offline to the authorization request and reconnect.

blockers.cause: The app has fewer than 50 linked users
blockers.fix: Wait until 50 users have linked, or fill in 'Request early review' with evidence.

composio.note: Composio's managed Dropbox app is fine for prototyping and internal use. Register your own app when you want your name and logo on the consent screen, a trimmed scope list, or production approval under your own app key. Your own app also works without review for up to 500 users while in Development status, but the two-week production deadline starts at 50 linked users. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config: the catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, while the probe used a v3 callback path.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit catalog lists managed OAuth2 for Dropbox, with a default scope set and the authorization and token URLs.
The App Console at dropbox.com/developers/apps is where developers create and manage apps; visiting it unauthenticated redirects to a Dropbox login page.
The App Console walks developers through registering the app, choosing permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret; redirect URIs are entered there too.

evidence.claim: Newly created apps start in Development status and can only be connected to the creator's own account; up to a limited number of other accounts can be added via 'Enable additional users'.
Dropbox's Developer Terms require a developer who wants to move an app into production to submit a production status request, which Dropbox may deny at its discretion.
The Developer Terms (effective March 1, 2025) bind the organization when a developer accepts on its behalf.
Development-status apps can link up to 500 total Dropbox users; once 50 users link, the developer has two weeks to apply for and receive production approval before further linking is frozen.
A production request is not reviewed until the app has linked at least 50 users; demos, hackathons, staging and internal tools can stay in development status.
The production application is submitted from the app info page in the App Console; it asks how the app uses the API, requires an uploaded app icon, and has a 'Request early review' field.
An app will be rejected if it does not follow the branding guidelines and terms, and Dropbox expects an app-specific privacy policy.
The Developer Terms require a privacy policy describing what user information is collected and how it is used and shared.
The Developer Terms impose security duties including HTTPS encryption in transit and prompt breach reporting.
Production review checks that the app does not request a permission broader than its functionality needs; planned broader permissions should be mentioned in the request.
The production readiness review ends in approval or denial; a denied app receives feedback and can resubmit.
Once an app has production status its name cannot be changed by the developer without a request through the developer contact page.
App names may not include the word Dropbox, any Dropbox product name, or anything similar.
The app logo must not look like a Dropbox logo; it is shown on the authorization page and must be submitted with the production application.
Marketing may not suggest a partnership with or endorsement by Dropbox.
Branding fields (app name, publisher, description, website URL, icons) are set in the App Console and used during production approval.
The permission type (App folder or Full Dropbox) cannot be switched on an existing app.
The redirect_uri must exactly match a registered value; non-localhost redirect URIs must use HTTPS.
The code flow exchanges the code at the token endpoint using the app key and secret; PKCE with S256 is recommended for public clients.
Access tokens are short-lived; a refresh token is issued only if token_access_type=offline is set.
Refresh tokens do not expire automatically and refresh requests do not return a new refresh token.
A user's approval remains valid until revoked, so expired access tokens can be renewed without user input.

Scopes are selected in the Permissions tab; if the request omits scopes, the consent page requests all selected scopes.
Dropbox advises requesting the least permission needed; over-requesting can affect app review.

evidence.claim: App folder access confines the app to its folder; production review scrutinizes Full Dropbox requests.
Wrapper/framework developers must have each downstream developer register their own app key.
Some app types are excluded, including copyright-infringing apps and publicly searchable file-sharing networks.
The Developer Terms bar using one access token to let multiple users access one Dropbox account and require Dropbox's own login page.
An older Dropbox support page says production requests are answered within a few business days; may not be current.
A community answer states development vs production status does not change access token expiry.
The Dropbox OIDC discovery document is live and advertises openid, profile and email scopes.
The Dropbox authorization endpoint rejects an unrecognized client_id with an unknown_client_id error page.
Dropbox may suspend or terminate developer access for material breach (30-day cure), legal requirement, or security reasons.

open_questions: Which Composio callback URL to register: the catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but the probe used a v3 callback path. Copy the one your auth config shows.
Dropbox publishes no list of sensitive or restricted scopes, and the findings don't show how particular scopes affect production review.
The current production review time is unverified. The 'few business days' figure comes from an old support page.
The exact access-token lifetime isn't documented. The 14400 seconds in the docs is only an example value.
Whether Composio's default contacts and file_requests scopes are available for every permission type was not checked.
The pages fetched mentioned no demo-video, security-assessment or domain-verification requirement, but that wasn't confirmed as policy.
Team (Business API) scopes and their access rules weren't researched.
